read.sections.0.text.note: 'Đô thị hóa' for urbanisation (not in KEY_TERMS.md); 'giao thông' for transport (covers roads, trains, boats; a reviewer may prefer 'phương tiện đi lại' or 'vận tải'). 'Kho lạnh' for cold-storage building. 'Thủ đô' for capital city.
read.sections.0.text.source: Most cities start small. A town often grows when something brings new jobs, such as a harbour, a railway or factories. Better transport also helps, because it lets people and goods move in and out more easily. Look at Bayview. In Year 8, a new road and a cold-storage building opened, so fish could stay fresh all the way to the capital city. That created 800 new jobs, and people moved to Bayview to do them. This kind of change is called urbanisation: more and more people come to live in towns and cities.
read.sections.0.text.back: Most cities start small. A town usually grows when something brings new jobs, like a harbour, a railway or factories. Better transport also helps, because it makes it easier for people and goods to come and go. Look at Bayview. In Year 8, a new road and a cold store were opened, so fish could be kept fresh all the way to the capital. That created 800 new jobs, and people moved to Bayview to do those jobs. This kind of change is called urbanisation: more and more people come to live in towns and cities.

read.sections.0.simpler.note: Check that 'đô thị hóa' (a hard word) is explained clearly enough in the last sentences.
read.sections.0.simpler.source: Most cities start small. A town can grow when new jobs come. A harbour, a railway or factories can bring jobs. Good transport helps people and goods move. Look at Bayview. In Year 8, a new road opened. A big cold room opened too. It kept fish fresh. This made 800 new jobs. People moved to Bayview for the jobs. This is called urbanisation. More people live in towns and cities.
read.sections.0.simpler.back: Most cities start small. A town can grow when there are new jobs. A harbour, a railway or factories can bring jobs. Good transport helps people and goods move. Look at Bayview. In Year 8, a new road was opened. A big cold store was also opened. It keeps fish fresh. This made 800 new jobs. People moved to Bayview to work. This is called urbanisation. More and more people live in towns and cities.

read.sections.1.heading.source: Real cities grew in similar ways
read.sections.1.heading.back: Real cities also grew in a similar way

read.sections.1.text.note: Real places: Nairobi and Kenya kept in Latin spelling (some books write Nai-rô-bi, Kê-ni-a); Thâm Quyến for Shenzhen; 'một khu đặc biệt dành cho kinh doanh' for a special area for business (the usual term is 'đặc khu kinh tế', not used because the English does not say 'economic zone'). The statement that the government made it a special area is factual in the English; keep it neutral.
read.sections.1.text.source: Many real cities grew in a similar way. Nairobi, the capital of Kenya, began in 1899 as a stop on a new railway. Workers and traders came, and the stop grew into a city. In 1980, only about 30,000 people lived in Shenzhen, in southern China. Then the government made it a special area for business. Factories opened, and millions of people moved there for work. Today it is one of the biggest cities in China. In both places, new jobs and transport made the population grow.
read.sections.1.text.back: Many real cities grew in a similar way. Nairobi, the capital of Kenya, began in 1899 as a stopping point on a new railway. Workers and traders flocked in, and the stopping point grew into a city. In 1980, only about 30,000 people lived in Shenzhen, in southern China. Then the government turned the place into a special zone for business. Factories opened, and millions of people moved there to work. Today it is one of China's biggest cities. In both places, new jobs and transport made the population rise.

read.sections.1.simpler.source: Real cities grew like this too. Nairobi is a big city in Kenya. It started in 1899 as a stop on a railway. Workers and traders came. The stop grew into a city. Shenzhen is a city in China. In 1980, it was small. Then many factories opened there. Millions of people came to work. Now it is one of China's biggest cities. In both places, jobs and transport made the population grow.
read.sections.1.simpler.back: Real cities also grew like this. Nairobi is a big city in Kenya. It began in 1899 as a stopping point on the railway. Workers and traders flocked in. The stopping point grew into a city. Shenzhen is a city in China. In 1980 it was small. Then many factories opened there. Millions of people came to work. Now it is one of China's biggest cities. In both places, jobs and transport made the population rise.

read.sections.2.text.note: 'Áp lực' for pressures, 'lợi ích' for benefits. 'Những người quy hoạch' for planners: check it is understood by 12-year-olds. 'Cơ sở hạ tầng' and 'dịch vụ' are used in their general senses.
read.sections.2.text.source: Growth can be good for a city, because a bigger city can have more jobs, schools, shops and buses. But more people also need more homes, clean water and health care. A service is help that people need, like a clinic or a school. Infrastructure means the basic systems a place needs, such as roads, water pipes and power lines. Both take time and money to build. In Year 15, Bayview has new houses, a school and bus routes. But people wait a long time at the only clinic, because it did not grow as fast as the population. Good planners watch for pressures like this and plan ahead.
read.sections.2.text.back: Growth can be good for a city, because a bigger city can have more jobs, schools, shops and buses. But more people also need more housing, clean water and health care. A service is help that people need, like a clinic or a school. Infrastructure is the basic systems a place needs, like roads, water pipes and power lines. Both take time and money to build. In Year 15, Bayview has new houses, a school and bus routes. But people have to wait a very long time at the only clinic, because it did not grow as fast as the population. Good planners keep an eye on pressures like this and make plans in advance.

read.sections.2.simpler.source: Growth can be good. A big city has more jobs, schools and buses. But more people need more things. They need homes and clean water. They need a service like a clinic. They need infrastructure, like roads and pipes. These take time to build. In Year 15, people wait a long time at the Bayview clinic. It did not grow as fast as the population. Planners try to see problems early.
read.sections.2.simpler.back: Growth can be good. A big city has more jobs, schools and buses. But more people need more things. They need housing and clean water. They need a service such as a clinic. They need infrastructure, like roads and water pipes. These things take time to build. In Year 15, people had to wait a very long time at Bayview's clinic. The clinic did not grow as fast as the population. Planners try to see problems early.

watch.summary.note: 'Phần lương thực dư' for extra food (surplus in KEY_TERMS is 'phần dư'). 'Xe kéo' for carts. 'Cách đưa rác thải đi' for ways to take away waste. The 'more than half' fact is from the English. | Review: 'xe kéo' for 'carts' usually means a hand-pulled rickshaw; 'xe bò' or 'xe ngựa' may be clearer.
watch.summary.source: The video starts with a fact: today, more than half of all people live in towns and cities. About 10,000 years ago, people began to farm. They could grow food, so they stayed in villages. Later, better farming made extra food. Not everyone had to farm, so some people did other jobs. Villages grew into cities. Trade grew too, with carts, ships, roads and ports. Much later, factories and new machines helped cities grow even bigger. Cities added police, fire services, roads and ways to take away waste. In the future, even more people will live in cities. The video says cities must give everyone enough food, toilets and schools. They must also protect the land. Ideas include rooftop gardens, tall buildings, and power from the sun and wind.
watch.summary.back: The video starts with a fact: today, more than half of the people in the world live in towns and cities. About 10,000 years ago, people started farming. They could grow their own food, so they stayed in villages. Later, better farming produced surplus food. Not everyone had to farm, so some people did other jobs. Villages grew into cities. Trade also grew, with carts, ships and boats, roads and harbours. A long time after that, factories and machines helped cities grow even more. Cities got more police, fire brigades, roads and ways to take rubbish away. In the future, even more people will live in cities. The video says cities must give people enough food, toilets and schools. Cities must also protect the land. Some ideas are rooftop gardens, tall buildings, and electricity from the sun and wind.
